CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain in both knees.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with complaints of bilateral knee pain. The pain began over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs. He describes the pain in both knees as equally severe. He has had some knee problems in the past but attributes the current pain to repetition and the weight of the boxes. The pain was severe enough to keep him up Saturday night. He has tried Tylenol and ice with minimal relief. He denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He reports that his kidney transplant is doing well, with recent follow-up with Dr. Gutierrez a couple of weeks ago showing nothing out of the ordinary. He is compliant with his immunosuppressive medications. He continues on Synthroid for hypothyroidism and denies fatigue or weight gain. He occasionally experiences elbow pain but nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, headaches, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (for polycystic kidneys)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications
Synthroid
Tylenol (over-the-counter, taken for knee pain)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, afebrile, heart rate and blood pressure fine. Heart: 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted, which appears stable compared to prior. Knees: Right knee shows edema and erythema with pain to palpation and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears fine without edema or erythema.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture. White blood cell count not elevated. Kidney function very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every six hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Patient advised to take it easy. If symptoms continue, will consider further imaging and possible referral to physical therapy.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.
3. Arthritis: Continue conservative management. Will refer to physical therapy if needed. Noted limitation in use of anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant.
